thread:
Maya Chen: Morning — quick kickoff: SylphEdge wants a joint perf/W + throughput sweep next Wed (on their lab hw). Need a condensed test matrix and who owns what. TL;DR: we provide model configs, eval set, telemetry hooks; they run kernel-flag builds and give power logs. @Luis can you confirm access flow? @Priya you'll own eval set?
Luis Ortega: Yup, I can handle access. Need the lab IPs + service account email. I'll open an SSH key stamp request with eng-infra.
Priya Nair: I'll assemble the eval set today. Plan: 100 short, 50 medium, 30 long prompts, plus a 10-example adversarial subset for quality regressions. Will push to s3://redwood-partner-evals/sylphedge/ by EOD.
Ben Holt: From SRE side: we should not give blanket root. Recommend service account with scoped roles: compute:ssh-run, storage:read-only for that bucket. Also enable audit logging for the test window.
Maya Chen: Acceptance criteria proposal: perf/W within 10% of our baseline for the pinned model variants; p95 latency not worse than +5% at target QPS; no higher error rate on the adversarial subset. If SylphEdge wants an extended power curve, we can add a heavy-run at 2x throughput.
Luis Ortega: For automation, I'll provide an endpoint template and a small wrapper script. Example run command to hand to partners:
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-3b --qps 50 --batch 8 --profile perf_watt --out ./results.json
```
Bench output will include: tokens/s, avg power (W), p50/p95 latency, kernel-flag name.
Priya Nair: Note on eval metrics: include embedding-based semantic similarity for the long prompts so we can detect hallucination drift. I'll include eval scripts in the bucket.
Maya Chen: Telemetry: we need timestamped power logs and the per-request token counts to reconcile per-token watt. Ask partners to use NTP-synced logger and include kernel trace tag. Example format: CSV with columns ts, watts_avg, watts_peak, board_temp, run_tag.
Ben Holt: I'll prepare the temporary IAM role and whitelist IPs. Also setting up a short-lived Prometheus scrape on the partner node is possible if they agree; otherwise we'll accept their CSV and a signed checksum.
Luis Ortega: Who's owning kernel flags matrix? I can draft the initial matrix: baseline (no flags), tokopt-fast-attn, quant-int8, kvcache-prefetch, and a combined optimal set. We should limit to 6 variants to keep runs manageable.
Priya Nair: Sounds good. Also we'll run each config 3x for stability. Add a warmup of 200 steps before measuring.
Maya Chen: Timeline: today — eval set + flag matrix draft; tomorrow — IAM + access; Mon — handoff doc + runbook; Wed — partner runs; Thu — results ingest + comparison. Is that realistic?
Ben Holt: Tight but doable. Make sure partner signs the NDAs for telemetry transfer. I'll attach the checklist to the handoff doc.
Luis Ortega: I'll create a GH repo redwood/sylphedge-bench with scripts and a combined `run_all.sh`. Will include a minimal example config: 
```json
{ "model": "redwood-3b", "qps": 50, "batch": 8, "variants": ["baseline","tokopt-fast-attn"] }
```
Maya Chen: Great — one more thing: reporting format — we want a CSV summary and a short markdown report highlighting perf/W delta and any latency regressions. I'll make a template and drop into the repo.
bench-bot: Created ticket PARTNER-7123 and invited @luis @priya @ben to the handoff doc.
Maya Chen: OK team — action items: Priya assemble evals + scripts; Luis repo + wrapper + flag matrix; Ben IAM + logging; I'll draft acceptance and reporting templates and coordinate with SylphEdge for lab window. Ping here when items are done. :rocket:
Luis Ortega: Ping — repo created: https://github.com/redwood/sylphedge-bench (private). I'll open a PR with the flag matrix in 30m.
Priya Nair: Eval set uploaded to s3://redwood-partner-evals/sylphedge/ -- files: short.jsonl, mid.jsonl, long.jsonl, adversarial.jsonl.
Ben Holt: IAM role created: sylph-bench-role, expiry 72h. Sent whitelisting email to SylphEdge ops.
Maya Chen: Perfect — I'll circulate the runbook and confirm Wed 09:00 PT lab start. Thanks everyone.
Luis Ortega: I'll also add a small sanity check script that verifies power log timestamps align with run time window (common gotcha).
Maya Chen: Great catch. If any partners ask about kernel build reproducibility, point them to our kernel-patches/README and note the git commit we tested.
bench-bot: Reminder scheduled — followup thread will auto-create at 1790123499 for results ingest.
